relevance_note: A letter reporting one girl with SSADH deficiency treated with Vigabatrin ('At 8 years old SSADH deficiency was diagnosed [4, patient 2]'), plus brief individual-level notes on two previously reported patients; no ALDH5A1 variant is mentioned.
method_note: Read by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory, values typed from my reading. The Markdown file also contains two unrelated letters from the same journal pages (caffeine intoxication in a neonate; VACTERL plus hydrocephalus); they were ignored. The paper names no gene and prints no variant, so the variants table is empty; the basis of the diagnosis is not stated (clinical_diagnosis_basis not reported). n_patients_reported left null because the schema counts patients with an ALDH5A1 variant and none is stated. The first-hand patient is the paper's 'Our patient' (label 'patient'); she is stated to be patient 2 of reference 4, recorded as a prior report. Two previously published patients are included as 'ref [2] patient' (Jaeken and coworkers; Vigabatrin response, CSF 4-HB fell 70%, GABA rose almost sixfold) and 'ref [1] patient' (Gibson et al.; no response, 'complete enzymatic block'); their only individual-level facts are treatment response and biochemistry, so their inclusion is a judgement call. The SSADH diagnosis of the ref [2] patient is implied only by context, so its disease label is 'not reported'. A garbled OCR passage ('a modnt  t nt avt  mnt set slightly from < 20 to 20–50', probably a developmental or IQ score) and post-treatment improvements were not recorded as features. Checklist 'intellectual disability' is marked observed from 'gross retardation of motor and psychosocial development' (no explicit intellectual disability statement). 'attention problems or ADHD' left not reported: the paper reports hyperactivity/restlessness but not attention problems or ADHD. The paper says aggressiveness 'may or may not be a manifestation of her inborn error of metabolism'; the behaviour is still recorded as observed. No contradictions found.
